prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Denver for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t objectively name one single “best” lawyer — the right lawyer depends on the facts of your case and who you feel comfortable working with. Instead, here’s a practical way to find the best Denver personal injury attorney for your car accident.

How to find the right lawyer
- Look for experience with car-accident cases (not general practice). Prefer attorneys who handle injury claims regularly and have trial experience.
- Check results: settlements and verdicts in similar cases, especially comparable injuries and liability issues.
- Verify credentials: Colorado Bar membership, peer-review ratings (Martindale‑Hubbell), Super Lawyers, Avvo, client reviews.
- Fee structure: most work on contingency (no fee unless you recover). Typical contingency ranges are about 33%–40% (confirm up front).
- Communication and accessibility: who will actually handle the file, how often you’ll get updates, and responsiveness.
- Local knowledge: experience with Denver courts, local judges and opposing insurers can help.

Resources to use
- Colorado Bar Association directory
- Avvo, Martindale‑Hubbell, Super Lawyers, Google and Yelp reviews
- Local referrals (friends, family, other attorneys)
- Better Business Bureau for complaints

What to ask at a free consultation
- How much of your practice is car-accident/personal injury?
- How many cases like mine have you handled and what were the outcomes?
- Do you have trial experience in Denver courts?
- Who will handle my case day-to-day?
- What are your fees and costs? Do you advance costs?
- How do you estimate the value and likely timeline?
- How will medical liens and insurance subrogation be handled?

What to bring to an initial meeting
- Police report, photos of the accident/damage/injuries
- Names/contact info for other drivers and witnesses
- Insurance info (yours and other party’s)
- Medical records and bills, treatment timeline
- Pay stubs if lost wages are an issue

Timing and deadlines
- Act promptly — Colorado’s general statute of limitations for personal injury is typically two years from the date of the injury, but there are exceptions (government claims, minors, etc.). So don’t wait.

If you’d like, I can:
- Pull together a short list (3–5) of highly rated Denver personal injury lawyers based on public ratings and recent results, or
- Help draft an email or list of questions for consultations.

If you want a curated list, tell me your ZIP code, a brief summary of the accident (date, injury severity, whether fault is disputed), and any preferences (trial-focused lawyer, bilingual, etc.).
